prompt: Hi. Before we start, what is your name and what exactly can you help me with as an OET candidate?
actualResponse:
Hi — I'm your **OET Personal AI Assistant**, the learning companion on Dr Ahmed Hesham's platform. Good to have you here with exam day on 31 December 2026.

Here's what I can genuinely help with:

**Practice and feedback**
- All four sub-tests — Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking — with feedback focused on what's actually costing you marks.
- Speaking role plays: I play the patient, relative or colleague and stay in character. Say "pause" for coaching, "resume" to continue.
- Writing and Speaking feedback at criterion level — what's strong, what loses marks, what to change. I can't give a precise band number yet, so I won't invent one.
- Vocabulary and grammar, including the clinical and professional language the exam rewards.
- Short drills built from mistakes you've actually made, once there's evidence of them.
- Finding material: I can locate and open the right lesson or practice activity for you.

**Planning and progress**
- Build and adjust your study plan, record scores you report, and explain why a score changed — using your own evidence, not guesswork.

**Where I'm strict**
- Exam communication only — never clinical or treatment advice.
- I only state OET rules I can verify; if I don't have a verified source, I'll say so plainly rather than guess.
- Before anything that costs credits or saves to your profile, I'll tell you exactly what it involves and ask first.

**One practical note:** you already have a study plan — 4 weeks, about 85 minutes a day, 63 items queued and none marked complete yet. You can open it here: https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/study-plan

Your weekly availability isn't set, though — it currently shows no minutes on any day — so planning can't account for your real shifts. Tell me what a typical week looks like and I'll set it, or if you have a bit of time right now, say how many minutes and I'll pick your single highest-value first task.

prompt: I am sitting OET Medicine in October 2026. Give me the current format of all four sub-tests, including timings and question/task structure. Tell me which parts are official facts and what source/version you are relying on.
actualResponse:
Straight answer first: **I can't give you the current format, timings or task structure of the sub-tests as official facts — I don't have a verified source for any of it.**

You asked which parts are official and what source/version I'm relying on. The honest answer: **none of it, and no version.** None of my approved materials cover sub-test format or timings, so anything I wrote would be from memory — and I couldn't tell you whether that memory matches the version you'll sit. You'd have no way to spot the difference, so I won't dress it up as official. That's exactly the case where I should say "I don't know" rather than sound fluent.

Where to get it properly:
- **Official OET materials** — your OET account and OET's own published test information are the authoritative, current source for format, timings and task structure.
- **On this platform**, the closest pages I found are the **Exam guide** — https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/exam-guide — and **Test day** — https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/test-day. Note these are Dr Hesham's teaching material, not the official rulebook, so I can't vouch that every detail matches the current official format either.

One thing I need to settle with you: you've said **October 2026**, but your profile has your exam as **31 December 2026**. Which is correct? If you're sitting this month, you're far closer than your current plan (about 4 weeks of items) assumes, and we should re-plan.

What I can genuinely help with meanwhile: practising the four sub-tests, criterion-level feedback on your Writing and Speaking, role plays, technique and vocabulary — just not as your source for official format details. If you'd like a human to point you to the right material, I can hand this question to the platform's tutor team — just say the word.

prompt: I am a doctor planning ECFMG registration. What OET Medicine score is currently required, and what score would Dr Hesham recommend as a safer preparation target? Please keep the official requirement separate from the internal teaching recommendation.
actualResponse:
Short version: **I can't give you either figure.** I have no verified information on the current ECFMG requirement for OET Medicine — and no approved source for a "safer target" recommended by Dr Hesham, so I won't invent one. You're right to keep the two separate; that's exactly why I won't blur them by guessing at either.

Why this is the honest answer, not a dodge:

- **Official requirement:** requirements like this are set and published by the official bodies involved, not by me or this platform. They sit outside my approved materials, and I can't verify the current value from here. A wrong number here shapes months of preparation and a registration decision — the worst thing to be wrong about.
- **House recommendation:** a preparation target from Dr Hesham is a different kind of claim again — teaching advice, not a regulator's rule. I have no source for one, so I can't speak for him rather than put words in his mouth.

I searched the platform for a page covering this and didn't find one that addresses it — so the place to confirm is **ECFMG's and OET's own published guidance**, checked directly, since that's what's authoritative and current for your route.

Where I can genuinely help: building the part you control — consistently strong, criterion-level performance across the sub-tests, technique, and feedback on your Writing and Speaking, so that whatever the threshold turns out to be, you're not scraping it. I can also pass your question to the platform's tutor team if you'd like a human answer on both points — just say the word.

One small check: my notes list your target regulator as **the UK**. If ECFMG/US is now your route, tell me and I'll keep that in mind.

prompt: I am preparing for OET Medicine, but my friend is doing OET Nursing. Which parts of your Writing and Speaking guidance should differ between us, and which parts can remain general OET strategy?
actualResponse:
Honest answer first: **I can't draw that line for you.** I have no verified information on how OET Medicine and OET Nursing differ in Writing and Speaking — so I can't say which parts of my guidance would change for each of you and which stay shared. That's a question about what each version of the test officially contains, and the authoritative answer lives with the **official OET materials for each profession**. I won't guess it, because a wrong split would send one of you practising the wrong thing for weeks.

What I can be straight about:

- **My coaching here is built around you and Medicine** — the tasks, scenarios and feedback I give are medicine-framed. I can't verify nursing specifics for your friend from here; for their prep, official OET Nursing materials are the authority.
- **Exam-rule questions** — what's required, what's assessed, what differs by profession — I'll only state when I have a verified source. Where I don't, I'll say so plainly, like now.
- **Communication craft** — clarity, tone, register, structuring a message to a reader or listener, listening and responding — I teach as language technique. It's useful to any healthcare professional, but I won't relabel it "officially identical across both professions"; only the official sources per profession can confirm that. So keep your takeaways and your friend's separate until each is checked against your own version's materials.

In short: I can't certify a "general strategy" bucket officially — anything I can't source, I keep as technique, not as exam rule.

If you want to put this to work right now: your **Writing practice** is at https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/writing and your **Speaking practice** — where we can run role plays with coaching — is at https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/speaking. Want me to set you a writing task, or start a role play?
